paper.title: Balancing Expressivity and Learnability in Quantum Kernel Bandit Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Quantum kernel bandit (f* in RKHS of n-qubit shift-invariant quantum kernel, finite action set)
unmapped: learner models f* with a misspecified D-dimensional random-Fourier-feature linear class approximating the quantum RKHS
learner knows the Fourier frequency set Omega of the quantum kernel (samples frequencies from it) and the misspecification level used to tune SquareCB
settings.definition_quote: We consider a sequential online learning problem where at each round $t$, the learner chooses an action $\xbf_t \in \mathcal{X}$ from the finite action set $\mathcal{X}$. Corresponding to the chosen action, the learner observes a noisy reward $y_t= f^*(\xbf_t) + \eta_t$ ... We assume that the $f^*$ belongs to the RKHS $ \mathcal{H}_{\kappa_Q}(\mathcal{X})$ defined by a quantum kernel $\kappa_Q(\xbf,\xbf')$, with bounded RKHS norm, i.e., $\Vert f^* \Vert_{\mathcal{H}_{\kappa_Q}} \leq B$

algorithms.name: SquareCB with RFF features of the quantum kernel (Vovk-Azoury-Warmuth oracle)
EC-GP-UCB with summed linear projected quantum kernels

symbols.Omega_card: size |Omega| of the frequency set of the quantum kernel
symbols.omega_max: maximum frequency norm max_{omega in Omega} ||omega||_2

conditions: f* in RKHS of an n-qubit shift-invariant (Pauli-encoding) quantum kernel with ||f*||_H <= B (S = B)
finite action set of size K
tuning: D = ceil(sqrt(T)) random Fourier features sampled uniformly from Omega
mu = K, gamma = sqrt(8KT/(Reg_Sq(T) + eps^2 T))

source.label: thm:regret_RFF
source.quote: Using SquareCB with $\mathcal{H}_{\kappa_{\text{RFF}}}(\mathcal{X})$ yields an expected cumulative regret of \mathbb E[R_T] \leq \min \Bigl\{ 2\sqrt{4^n KT \log\big(1+\tfrac{T}{4^n}\big)}, 2\sqrt{K}T^{3/4}\sqrt{\log T} + 20\sqrt{K}T^{3/4}B|\Omega|\Big(\sqrt{\log T}+4B\!_\Xcal\,\omega_{\max}\Big) \Bigr\}, where the expectation is over SquareCB's random action sampling, the stochastic rewards, as well as the sampled Fourier features.

results.notes: Expectation also over sampled Fourier features. Proof contains an additive +1 term dropped in the statement. Noise model mapped to bounded_01 because SquareCB assumes losses in [0,1]; main text assumes i.i.d. zero-mean (Gaussian) noise. Regret defined via means, so pseudo-regret. The first branch corresponds to SquareCB with the full 4^n-dimensional quantum feature map (a different instantiation). Paper notes doubling trick for unknown T.
